findings.title: Bootstrap admission depends on an outcome that cannot yet exist.
findings.evidence: Integration calls proposedDecision before the financial journey. Classifier lines 48–51 already require independent final recovery and allFinancialCasesComplete. A qualifying native failure cannot proceed under this specification without inventing completion. The rejection helper at line 46 can also report rawStrict PASS for missing evidence or a financial failure when the ledger array is empty.
findings.requiredCorrection: Split provisional native admission from final aggregate. First verify complete bootstrap/session/asset evidence for the current phase plus exact eligible IDs, zero other already-observed failures, and checkpoint native rawStrict status. Native admission is never a full PASS. Then run strict enabled/financial phases with the unchanged fatal checks. After drain, recovery independently rechecks every ledger and exact native IDs, all required finance/control evidence, the decision hash and fresh run lock; only then compute aggregate and process exit. Empty/incomplete/unverified supplied data never yields raw PASS. Show separately network raw strictness and whole validation, or use UNKNOWN/FAIL when incomplete.

findings.title: The native declaration-to-bytes mapping is not actually bound in the data model.
findings.evidence: Artifact contains scope, generation, browser config, pathname and digests, but neither document, loader, full declaration token nor map entry for the native or enabled render. Lines 64–65 compare generation/path/digests but cannot prove that the failed native request was declared against that mapping. Distinct full tokens are correct: pinned Next app-render.js:836,1242, get-asset-query-string.js:13–26 and required-scripts.js:22–71 add a per-render decimal v. Evidence for one webpack path alone cannot authenticate every per-render variant.
findings.requiredCorrection: Store two explicit render → declared full-URL-token → frozen mapping-entry → compiled-byte-digest records, bound to run/context/document/loader and stable build generation. Within each document match declaration, PW and CDP uniquely on exact full-URL/context/hop without exposing the actual query. Across contexts require the exact reviewed webpack path, actor/route, relevant declaration attributes and verified immutable content identity. Only none or one renderer-generated numeric v may differ; reject unrecognized or unproven cache-buster, rebuild/drift or additional query dimensions. Compare the successful enabled response bytes and the exact V8-covered script identity to that digest, with positive execution and complete zero native execution capture. Do not invent response bytes for a blocked request. Capture the real build output after any necessary prerender/compile, freeze it before the measured documents and verify after. No stable association means UNAVAILABLE.

findings.title: Six independent labels do not prove three genuine login journeys or distinct counterpart documents.
findings.evidence: Each Session is checked only against one native context/scope (lines 63–67). The login and landing entries for an actor can come from different browser contexts, and the enabled counterpart’s identity is not independently session-verified. usedCounterparts at line 59 uses context+document+requestID+hop, so the same counterpart document with a different request ID can be reused. Positive role/org labels alone do not establish that the primary tenant, other tenant and staff visited the required actual pages.
findings.requiredCorrection: Use one verified native login-chain receipt per actor; both its scopes must reference the same actor/context and ordered main-frame document chain, actual pointer POST, redirects, final document and current intended session/consent/org. Distinguish the two tenants even when their org matches. Use one separately verified JS-enabled actor/context for the matched login and landing documents; bind the actor, route and selected org of the authenticated landing, not a label alone. A real soft-navigation /t Fetch cannot stand in for a landing document. A separate normal authenticated direct document visit can provide counterpart evidence but never replace the real enabled login verdict. Count all candidates before filtering; enforce unique counterpart document/context and request identity across scopes, reject conflicting/duplicate/extra events, missing receipts, ambiguous joins and all enabled cancellations.

findings.title: The policy parser is conservatively scoped; feasibility on the real app is not yet proved.
findings.evidence: policyAllows accepts only actual absence or complete single-directive self-only policies; it rejects all nonces, integrity attributes, additional directives and all non-self report-only policies. This is safe as an explicitly unavailable result, not proof that real documents qualify. No CSP declaration was found in inspected src/middleware.ts, next.config.ts or public/_headers; these files do not establish effective response/meta policies or intermediary/dev behavior. The previous product run did not capture them.
findings.requiredCorrection: Collect actual effective policy at the moment of each script/preload, preserving all distinct enforced response/meta policies and reporting-only presence; capture element/initiator and protected attributes before the request or reconcile from immutable response/parser data. Do not persist raw CSP, nonces or query strings. For the first implementation keep the small exact parser, or support a specifically reviewed actual template: script-src-elem → script-src → default-src, intersection of enforced policies, strict handling of nonce/strict-dynamic/integrity/initiator, report-only cannot grant or deny. For a supported nonce template require a per-document actual element/policy match in memory; compare effective permission for the asset, not nonce literals across documents. Any unsupported rule, unknown ordering, blocked policy or inconsistent evidence returns UNAVAILABLE. No general-purpose CSP reimplementation or speculative eligibility is required.

findings.title: The implementation must bind the approved note, not require approval of this old proposal.
findings.evidence: V2 predates Ron’s decision, asks for approval of its own manifest, and uses a top-level self-supplied manifestDigest compared to a phase witness. Domain separation and hardwired role keys are described but not implemented. Six signing roles add complexity without establishing the truth of browser, CSP or asset observations.
findings.requiredCorrection: Use the approved note SHA as policy authority and bind the **implementation** manifest, verified candidate, run nonce, helper/asset/browser freeze and mode separately in a parent-owned lock. Compare to independent expected values, not merely two matching input fields. A single pinned supervisor and private run directory, durable raw observer journals, parent-owned atomic phase manifests binding bytes/counts/hashes, and independent post-drain source/receipt/DB re-evaluation suffice under the locked local-process trust boundary. A self-reported hash alone is not independent evidence; recovery must verify raw journals/coverage/maps/session facts, not trust signed PASS booleans. Keep sensitive HMAC material memory-only. No six signing services or new user decision is necessary for an implementation remaining inside the approved note.
